info.title: viz tenant control plane
info.description: Keys, dashboards and their revisions, proposed changes, settings and the audit log of one tenant. The tenant is always the one the credential belongs to: no path, query or body takes a tenant, and a request that names one is refused. Errors are problem details with a "code" and a "fix". Every write accepts "dryRun": true. Lists page with an opaque "next" cursor.

post.description: A whole viz.dashboard/v1 spec for a person to review and apply. It is validated (422 invalid-dashboard with each error) and its id must be free (409 dashboard-exists or dashboard-deleted). Nothing is created until it is applied, which needs the right to create dashboards directly (see whoami mayApply). The same caller sending the same spec again while its proposal is open gets that proposal back: 200, outcome "unchanged", nothing written.

post.summary: Apply a proposal, whole or in part
post.description: Creates a normal revision attributed to the caller, with the proposer recorded. "changes" selects a subset by name. Refused with 409 needs-rebase when the dashboard moved and the changes no longer fit, and with 403 self-apply for an agent applying its own proposal unless agentsMayApply is true. A proposal of kind create is applied whole (no "changes", no base revision) and makes revision 1 of the new dashboard; it needs the right to create dashboards directly, so an agent is refused with 403 agents-may-not-apply unless agentsMayApply is true, and 409 dashboard-exists when the id was taken meanwhile. Applying twice is 409 proposal-closed, with appliedNumber.

post.summary: Approve an application's OAuth request (the consent step)
post.description: The page at /oauth/authorize shows what an application (an MCP client) asks for and a "request" handle. A person approves it here, with a key of kind "key" holding admin (an agent key is refused with 403 approver-not-a-person). The grant holds the scopes asked for (or the subset in "scopes") that the approving key itself holds; admin counts for the dashboards scopes. The answer's "redirect" is the application's callback with the code, state and iss: open it in the browser that started the connection, within codeExpiresAt. dryRun: true shows exactly what would be granted and issues no code. Bounds per tenant: 50 clients, 50 live grants, 20 approvals an hour (429), and a key per grant counts against the key cap.

apiKey.description: Authorization: Bearer viz_<keyId>_<secret>. The scopes listed per operation are alternatives: any one is enough.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code, e.g. stale-revision, needs-rebase, self-apply, missing-scope.

detail.description: What went wrong, in a sentence.

fix.description: What the caller should do next.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem details. Some codes add fields: stale-revision adds currentRevision, currentNumber, changedUnderneath, revisionsSince; invalid-dashboard adds errors; needs-rebase adds review.

mayApply.description: Whether this caller's direct dashboard writes (create, patch, revert, delete, restore, owner, and applying a proposal that creates a dashboard) take effect, rather than being refused or turned into a proposal. False without dashboards:apply (or admin), and for an agent while the tenant's agentsMayApply is false.

Scope.description: admin and dashboards:* are checked by this API; write and read by ingest and the query service; monitors:* by the ruler. Each service checks its own scopes; any scope reaches GET /whoami here.

prefix.description: viz_<keyId>: the public part of the key. The secret is never returned after creation.

anyOf.description: Set while a rotated-out secret is still inside its overlap.
Null until the data path reports usage for this key.
Samples written with this key in the last 24 h, to the hour. Null until usage is reported.
The full key, viz_<keyId>_<secret>. Shown in this response only; null in a dry run.

KvState.description: Whether the change has been written to KV for the data path. "pending" is retried within 30 s.

revision.description: Content hash of the current spec; use it as baseRevision or If-Match.

anyOf.description: From thresholds evaluated on data. Null unless the deployment wires the state hook.

name.description: Unique within the proposal; a reviewer accepts changes by name.

reason.description: Why; shown next to the diff.

items.description: One line per change, in words.

spec.description: viz.dashboard/v1 (only on GET of one revision).

kind.description: patch: named changes to an existing dashboard. create: a whole new dashboard, applied whole; baseRevision is "" and baseNumber 0, changes is empty.

dashboard.description: The dashboard changed, or for kind create the id of the dashboard it creates.

items.description: A Change; in lists, "ops" is the number of operations.

spec.description: Kind create, when one proposal is shown: the proposed viz.dashboard/v1 spec.

kind.description: Present for a proposal that creates a dashboard.

exists.description: Kind create: a dashboard (live or deleted) holds the id now, so it cannot be applied.

moved.description: The dashboard has changed since the proposal's base revision.

needsRebase.description: It moved and the changes no longer fit: an op fails, the result is invalid, or a change touches something edited since.

items.description: The diff against the CURRENT revision, in words.

anyOf.description: What applies: the value, or the default when never set.
The KV key the data path reads, if any.

OAuthScope.description: The scopes an OAuth grant may hold (contracts/oauth.ts OAUTH_SCOPES): those the agent surface checks. Never admin, write, monitors:write or monitors:ack.

status.description: suspended: its key is disabled, so the resource refuses its tokens until the key is enabled again.

name.description: The application's own name for itself; not verified.

resource.description: The audience: the resource its tokens are for (the MCP endpoint).

expiresAt.description: The grant ends then, whatever happens.

anyOf.description: person, client, code-reuse, refresh-reuse, wrong-client, not-exchanged, idle, approver-gone or expired.
